state_variables.protocol_meaning: Handle identifying the authentication session, assigned by TPM during StartAuthSession and verified by host in subsequent commands.

evidence.reason: auth->handle = tpm_buf_read_u32(buf, &offset); — handle is read from TPM response buffer (public, authenticated by TPM).
if (handle == auth->handle && auth->attrs == a) — handle is compared against buffer value for session matching.

assumptions: Handle is assigned by TPM and is public; no confidentiality required.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Offset in command buffer where session starts (before fill) or session index in response (after fill). Internal bookkeeping, not a protocol value.

evidence.reason: if (auth->session != tpm_buf_length(buf)) — used to track buffer position for session appending.
auth->session += 4; — updated as handles are appended.

assumptions: This is an implementation offset, not a protocol message element.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Nonce generated by host for session, used in HMAC and key derivation. Must be fresh and unpredictable but is sent in cleartext.

evidence.reason: get_random_bytes(nonce, sizeof(nonce)); memcpy(auth->our_nonce, nonce, sizeof(nonce)); — generated fresh with random bytes.
tpm_buf_append_u16(buf, SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE); tpm_buf_append(buf, nonce, SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE); — appended to command buffer (public).

assumptions: Nonce is public (sent in cleartext) but must be fresh and unpredictable.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Nonce generated by TPM for session, used in HMAC and key derivation. Received in response buffer.

evidence.reason: memcpy(auth->tpm_nonce, &buf->data[offset], sizeof(auth->tpm_nonce)); — read from TPM response buffer.
memcpy(auth->tpm_nonce, &buf->data[offset_s], len); — updated from response during check.

assumptions: Nonce is public (received in cleartext) but must be fresh and unpredictable.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Salt value derived from ECDH shared secret using KDFe. Used as input to session key derivation. Must remain secret.

evidence.reason: tpm2_KDFe(auth->salt, "SECRET", x, chip->null_ec_key_x, auth->salt); — derived from ECDH shared secret.
tpm2_KDFa(auth->salt, sizeof(auth->salt), "ATH", auth->tpm_nonce, auth->our_nonce, sizeof(auth->session_key), auth->session_key); — used as key material for session key derivation.

assumptions: Salt is derived from ECDH and must remain secret; it is never sent in cleartext.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Session key derived from salt and nonces using KDFa. Used for HMAC and encryption. Must remain secret.

evidence.reason: tpm2_KDFa(auth->salt, sizeof(auth->salt), "ATH", auth->tpm_nonce, auth->our_nonce, sizeof(auth->session_key), auth->session_key); — derived from salt and nonces.
hmac_sha256_init_usingrawkey(&hctx, auth->session_key, sizeof(auth->session_key) + auth->passphrase_len); — used as HMAC key.

assumptions: Session key is derived and must remain secret; it is never sent in cleartext.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Optional passphrase provided by caller for session authorization. Must remain secret.

evidence.reason: if (passphrase_len) memcpy(auth->passphrase, passphrase, passphrase_len); — copied from caller-provided buffer.

assumptions: Passphrase is caller-provided secret; its confidentiality is assumed.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Length of the optional passphrase. May reveal passphrase presence but not content.

evidence.reason: auth->passphrase_len = passphrase_len; — set from caller-provided value.

assumptions: Length is caller-provided; may be considered public but reveals passphrase presence.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: AES encryption key derived from session key and nonces using KDFa. Used for parameter encryption/decryption. Must remain secret.

evidence.reason: aes_prepareenckey(&auth->aes_key, auth->scratch, AES_KEY_BYTES); — key is prepared from scratch buffer which contains KDFa output.
tpm2_KDFa(auth->session_key, ..., "CFB", auth->our_nonce, auth->tpm_nonce, AES_KEY_BYTES + AES_BLOCK_SIZE, auth->scratch); — scratch contains derived key material.

assumptions: AES key is derived and must remain secret; it is never sent in cleartext.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Session attributes (e.g., decrypt, encrypt, audit) set by host and included in HMAC computation. Public but integrity-protected.

evidence.reason: auth->attrs = attributes; — set from caller-provided attributes.
tpm_buf_append_u8(buf, auth->attrs); — appended to command buffer (public).
hmac_sha256_update(&hctx, &auth->attrs, 1); — included in HMAC computation.

assumptions: Attributes are public but integrity-protected via HMAC.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Command code (ordinal) of the TPM command being authorized. Included in HMAC computation. Public but integrity-protected.

evidence.reason: auth->ordinal = head->ordinal; — saved from command header.
sha256_update(&sctx, (u8 *)&head->ordinal, sizeof(head->ordinal)); — included in HMAC computation.

assumptions: Ordinal is public but integrity-protected via HMAC.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Array of handles for objects referenced in the command. Used to retrieve names for HMAC computation. Public but integrity-protected.

evidence.reason: auth->name_h[slot] = handle; — stored from command handle.
if (auth->name_h[i] != handle) — compared against buffer handle for verification.

assumptions: Handles are public but integrity-protected via HMAC.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Array of names (hashed public areas) for objects referenced in the command. Used in HMAC computation. Public but integrity-protected.

evidence.reason: if (name) memcpy(auth->name[slot], name, name_size_alg); — stored from retrieved name.
sha256_update(&sctx, auth->name[i], ret); — included in HMAC computation.

assumptions: Names are public but integrity-protected via HMAC.

state_variables.protocol_meaning: Scratch buffer used for temporary storage of derived key material (AES key + IV). Not a protocol value.

evidence.reason: tpm2_KDFa(auth->session_key, ..., "CFB", auth->our_nonce, auth->tpm_nonce, AES_KEY_BYTES + AES_BLOCK_SIZE, auth->scratch); — used as output buffer for KDF.
aes_prepareenckey(&auth->aes_key, auth->scratch, AES_KEY_BYTES); — used as input for AES key preparation.

assumptions: Scratch buffer is implementation-only; its contents are derived from session key and nonces.
